head: f1646890e54be4919e5b134202840d88cbb23562
claim: a person links a ChatGPT account in their own app and the provider's answer comes back through the installed @byokit/accounts package

steps.start: a fresh consumer app with no package installed and no account linked
steps: install the shipped @byokit/accounts package into the app
the app links a ChatGPT account by device code: it shows a code and the person approves it
the app reads the account status
the app asks the provider a question and prints the answer it gets back
steps.result: the installed package answers: "ChatGPT is connected." and the answer "You said: Plan my day"

steps.start: an app with the previous released @byokit/accounts version installed from the npm registry
steps: the person links a ChatGPT account by device code and gets the provider's answer back
the app upgrades the installed package in place, over the version it had
the person links a ChatGPT account again and gets the provider's answer back through the upgraded package
steps.result: the upgraded package answers: "ChatGPT is connected." and the answer "You said: Plan my day"

verdicts.seen: I read all 8 lines of the capture. The status line reads 'ChatGPT is connected.' and the streamed and answer lines both read 'You said: Plan my day', which shows the linked account's answer coming back through @byokit/accounts@0.30.0. The 'not offered' and 'no account' lines are error paths for other cases, not contradictions of the positive result. The outcome names one part, so parts and covers are empty.

I read all three sections of the capture: the 0.29.0 baseline, the in-place upgrade step, and the core journey on @byokit/accounts@0.30.0. The upgraded run shows package @byokit/accounts@0.30.0, sign-in waiting code MOCK-10001, status ChatGPT is connected, and answer 'You said: Plan my day', which matches linking an account and getting the provider's answer back through the installed package. The provider is the kit's local stand-in rather than real ChatGPT, which is the only real gap against the outcome's wording. The outcome names one part, so parts and covers stay empty.
